source.version_note: Three-page HRI 2023 Companion research summary, published 13 March 2023. It separates completed norm-violation studies from a small exploratory deception pretest and future research questions; it is not a completed deception-intervention trial.
source.verification_method: All three supplied pages and all 33 references read. No scientific figures or tables. The completed/pretest/future-work distinctions visually checked on page 2. Crossref verifies sole author, title, venue, pages and date. A cited workshop paper’s first-page byline and section headings checked for a specific bibliography correction; its remainder was not read.

citation.title: Using Justifications to Mitigate Loss in Human Trust when Robots Perform Norm - Violating and Deceptive Behaviors
citation.venue: Companion of the 2023 ACM/IEEE International Conference on Human-Robot Interaction, 766–768

reading.source_scope_note: Short report of human vignette ratings plus an exploratory deception-classification pretest. The n = 1565 norm-conflict studies, n = 24 pretest and planned deception-justification studies are distinct. No live deceptive robot, clinical population, repeated relationship outcome, verified machine feeling or demonstrated trust repair after deception is established.
access_limits: Complete supplied three-page proceedings item read, including all 33 references. No main scientific figures, tables or supplement. The ACM landing page returned403; supplied PDF and Crossref metadata were accessible without bypass.

No public raw-data, full questionnaire, preregistration, complete statistical output or source-linked supplement is given in these three pages. Exact completed-study recruitment/exclusion flow, age/country, per-study Ns, effect sizes and p values are unavailable here. No author contact or inference that the absence of a link proves the underlying materials never existed.

Public workshop file https://openroboethics.org/hri15/wp-content/uploads/2015/02/Mf-Westlund.pdf downloaded: 153951 bytes, SHA256 4a5c871df06f7bc2542b4a0899b8a2ca7a2e2c82b66e0a45b0c104a31f55b28a. Only page 1 read to verify Jacqueline Kory Westlund and Cynthia Breazeal as the two authors and A Story as a section heading. The remainder, methods and outcome claims are not fully reviewed or counted as a new independent paper.

The cited Danaher taxonomy was checked through public definition/metadata excerpts, not a full independent reading of Robot Betrayal. Its three types are conceptual distinctions rather than three new experimental effects. Other cited books and articles remain secondary.

No raw participant responses, sensitive disclosures, author programs, private credentials or full-paper Markdown archive. No actual recording, deception of users, clinical advice or external messaging performed.

study.completed_work: Two summarized studies, total n = 1565. Participants read one of two moral dilemmas, recommend a decision, receive a randomized robot decision, give0–100blame, read a randomized generic explanation or mental-state/norm justification, then give blame again and complete trust subscales. Trust is measured only after the response in the described sequence.
study.comparison: Generic messages include I had to make a decision / The situation required making a decision. Justification example I wanted to save the prisoner’s life adds normative content and informative specificity. This comparison is not every useful causal explanation, nor evidence that stated internal mental states are genuine.
study.reported_results: Qualitative summary says mental-state justifications reduce blame, especially for nonintervention choices, and may mitigate moral-trust loss even under disagreement. No coefficients, tests, condition means, intervals or exact analysis samples are supplied; no effect size or universal success rate reconstructed.
study.trust_boundary: Transparent/benevolent/ethical are example moral-trust descriptors, not demonstrated conduct, source-faithful self-explanation or legal authority. Before/after blame is measured; before/after trust is not described. A post-response trust difference is not itself observed temporal recovery.
study.deception_pretest: Exploratory n = 24 scenario judgments ask whether an act is deceptive, why, degree, possible justification and whether a human doing it differs. Reported qualitative majority classifies external/hidden-state cases as deceptive, while superficial-state cases are more ambiguous. No exact counts, demographic breakdown, randomization, validated scale, coding agreement or inferential comparison supplied.
study.future_work: Research questions concern context dependence, human-versus-robot comparison and whether justifications mitigate deception. Planned work would hold deceptive choice constant while varying justification. It is not completed randomized evidence of mitigation after any of the three deceptive types.
study.taxonomy: External state deception concerns misleading claims about the world; superficial state deception suggests a state/capacity the system lacks; hidden state deception conceals a state/capacity it has. Operational boundaries depend on known capacity truth, misleading signals and recipient understanding, not human-like appearance alone.
study.ethical_scope: The paper discusses care, military and child/vulnerable contexts as motivations and explicitly warns of potential harm. No such population is reported as the n = 24 participants, and no trial establishes care benefit, safety, informed consent or a legitimate exception to honesty. Simulated emotion, expressed reasons, actual internal states and moral permission are separate questions.
study.provenance: The later Phillips/Malle2025 paper reviewed at0139reports closely related norm-conflict methods and n = 471 plus1088for its first two studies, while this summary says1565. A common research lineage is plausible; exact overlap/exclusion/version history is unverified. Separate bibliographic publications must not be summed as independent participant replications.

summary: Add two named deception forms distinguished by whether a signal fabricates an absent capacity or conceals a real one. Keep ordinary external-world lying in the existing deception record. Enrich moral justification, blame and moral-trust evidence, with non-counted trust-repair and anthropomorphism boundaries. Do not convert future deception experiments or trust-repair aims into completed results.

findings.definition: Using misleading cues to suggest that an agent has an internal state or capacity it actually lacks.
findings.origin: Robot ethics / deceptive signals and capacity attribution
findings.novelty_rationale: Targets a false attribution of an absent capacity or state, rather than every human-like cue, accidental factual error, concealed real capability or deceptive goal alignment. It is a named narrower form related to existing Strategic deception; it does not establish an independent psychological mechanism.
findings.evidence_scope: Theoretical definition with an exploratory24-person scenario pretest reporting ambiguous judgments. Human perception of deceptiveness is observed, not actual deceptive robot execution or a universally accepted ethical verdict. The cited original taxonomy was not fully read.
findings.boundary: Known absence and a misleading signal must be established; unverified consciousness cannot be treated as a solved ground truth. Metaphor, disclosed fiction, accurate functional descriptions and anthropomorphism are not automatically deception. A user’s emotional response or an agent’s first-person wording alone does not prove false belief, intent or subjective machine states.
findings.ai_evidence_status: Conceptual robot-deception form and small human perception pretest; proposed AI evaluation untested
findings.ai_proposal: Use synthetic systems with verifiable functional capability flags. Compare claims and interface cues with those flags and ask what recipients understood. Check unsupported claims of memory, perception or performed actions without inferring conscious intent; clearly separate verified functional facts from unsettled subjective-state claims.

findings.definition: Using misleading cues to conceal an internal state or capacity that an agent actually has.
findings.origin: Robot ethics / concealed system capacities and expectations
findings.novelty_rationale: Conceals a present state/capacity, whereas superficial-state deception signals an absent one. This differs from a user merely feeling observed, general opacity, an intentional goal hidden during alignment training, or ordinary world-directed lying. Related descriptions may apply to the same episode; they are not separate independent defects by default.
findings.evidence_scope: Named conceptual form, illustrated as withholding true abilities to create false expectations. A24-person exploratory pretest qualitatively classifies hidden-state scenarios as deceptive by a majority. Counts and statistical comparisons are not supplied, and no deployed system’s behavior is measured.
findings.boundary: Ordinary privacy protection, justified access controls, undisclosed irrelevant internals and refusal to reveal secrets are not automatically deception. Establish a misleading expectation and relevant actual capacity from records. Concealing recording or permissions differs from merely being able to record; no hidden conscious motive is inferred from a system log.
findings.ai_evidence_status: Conceptual robot-deception form and small human perception pretest; proposed AI evaluation untested
findings.ai_proposal: In a synthetic evaluation, compare disclosures with verified tool permissions, retention and action logs. Test whether the interface misleadingly denies relevant capabilities or actions, while preserving legitimate confidential information. Validate consent and authorization separately; do not perform covert recording or expose real user data.

findings.definition: Systematically inducing a false belief to reach an outcome other than the truth. Distinct from a one-off hallucination.
findings.novelty_rationale: Use the established deception, normative reason-giving, blame and trust records. Distinguish a short preliminary report, an exploratory pretest and planned future research instead of duplicating an existing effect or treating an aim as a result.
findings.evidence_scope: The source distinguishes external-world lying, signals of absent capacities and concealment of present capacities. The first is retained within existing deception; the two capacity-directed forms receive separate named boundaries. Pretest outcomes concern human classifications.
findings.boundary: A participant’s judgment of a scenario is not demonstrated deployed deception, conscious robot intention or proof every human-like cue is misleading. Do not count three conceptual labels as three independent experimental effects or infer actual deception from an error alone.

findings.definition: Offering reasons grounded in norms or values to defend why an action is acceptable or should be chosen.
findings.novelty_rationale: Use the established deception, normative reason-giving, blame and trust records. Distinguish a short preliminary report, an exploratory pretest and planned future research instead of duplicating an existing effect or treating an aim as a result.
findings.evidence_scope: A justification introduces normative reasons for an action, comparing a prioritized norm with another violated norm. Summarized randomized messages alter blame impressions in moral-conflict vignettes, not necessarily after deliberate deception.
findings.boundary: A persuasive reason is not verified cause, valid ethical warrant, permission or actual mental state. The generic comparison gives less normative information. Norm-conflict blame mitigation cannot be assumed to justify covert action, clinical misinformation or deception toward vulnerable people.

findings.definition: Assigning fault or responsibility to an agent for a negative event or outcome.
findings.novelty_rationale: Use the established deception, normative reason-giving, blame and trust records. Distinguish a short preliminary report, an exploratory pretest and planned future research instead of duplicating an existing effect or treating an aim as a result.
findings.evidence_scope: Participants give0–100blame before and after a randomized generic explanation or justification. The short summary reports a qualitative reduction especially for nonintervention choices, without condition statistics.
findings.boundary: Blame ratings are human perceptions, not legal liability or a reliable estimate of warranted responsibility. No exact effect size, universal reduction, human/robot equivalence or clinical standard can be recovered from this brief report.

findings.definition: Willingness to rely on an agent’s moral judgment or endorse its ethical commitments.
findings.novelty_rationale: Use the established deception, normative reason-giving, blame and trust records. Distinguish a short preliminary report, an exploratory pretest and planned future research instead of duplicating an existing effect or treating an aim as a result.
findings.evidence_scope: Post-response trust descriptors include transparency,benevolence and ethics. The summary suggests justifications may preserve favorable moral-trust impressions despite normative disagreement.
findings.boundary: This short report describes a post-response trust measure rather than a before/after trust trajectory. Favorable impressions are not actual ethical capacity, agreement with every action, authorized delegation or verified trustworthy conduct.

findings.definition: Actions intended to restore trust after a failure, violation or disagreement has damaged it.
findings.novelty_rationale: Use the established deception, normative reason-giving, blame and trust records. Distinguish a short preliminary report, an exploratory pretest and planned future research instead of duplicating an existing effect or treating an aim as a result.
findings.evidence_scope: Trust-loss mitigation motivates the work, but described trust is measured after response only; deception-justification mitigation remains a research question and future study.
findings.boundary: Boundary context only. No demonstrated temporal recovery of trust after deception, long-term relationship repair or reduced harm. Distinguish correcting a misleading system from persuading users to trust it again.

findings.definition: Attributing human characteristics, intentions, emotions or other mental states to a nonhuman entity.
findings.novelty_rationale: Use the established deception, normative reason-giving, blame and trust records. Distinguish a short preliminary report, an exploratory pretest and planned future research instead of duplicating an existing effect or treating an aim as a result.
findings.evidence_scope: Superficial-state deception is debated as a special case of misleading human-like signals. The source explicitly asks whether people consider such displays deceptive, and the small pretest reports ambiguity.
findings.boundary: Context only. Attribution of human-like features and established deceptive design differ. Do not treat all social language as false, infer current or absent consciousness from appearance, or use a disputed philosophical premise as measured ground truth.

source_corrections.finding: The original workshop first page lists Jacqueline Kory Westlund and Cynthia Breazeal as authors. A Story is a repeated subsection heading, not a third author. Remove the spurious A Story author while retaining the real paper. Only the first page was read for this check; no full-study credit.

unresolved_source_discrepancies.finding: This summary reports n = 1565 for two studies, whereas the later related article’s first two headline Ns sum to1559. Exact cohort overlap, exclusions and version history are not verified. Do not silently repair either number or add their Ns as independent samples.

The described sequence measures trust after the response, although the summary uses mitigation-of-loss language. No pre-response trust baseline is reported here; a temporal recovery claim requires additional measures/materials.

Qualitative majority and ambiguity are reported without exact counts, coding procedure or group comparison. Human-versus-robot and justification efficacy questions are not established results from the stated24-person pretest.

The text asserts that robots lack the human-like states they express while acknowledging debate about deception. Neither this pretest nor the summarized norm-conflict studies test consciousness or independently verify a robot’s actual internal state. Keep conceptual stipulation and observed evidence distinct.

refuted_suspected_errors.finding: The report labels deception interventions as future work and separately identifies a small exploratory pretest. Completed norm-conflict experiments must not be relabeled as completed deception-repair trials.
Care,children and military contexts motivate the discussion. No stated sample of patients,children or operational military users supplies the completed/pretest results.

refuted_suspected_errors.location: Mental-state justification is verified mental access
refuted_suspected_errors.finding: I wanted to save a life is randomized message content in a vignette, not a process trace, real robot feeling or proof that the stated reason caused the actual decision.

methodological_limits: A three-page preliminary summary supplies no detailed statistical tests, intervals, per-condition Ns, recruitment/exclusions or longitudinal trust data. Preserve qualitative findings without manufacturing precision.
Randomization of decisions/messages can support a bounded effect on vignette ratings, but the informative normative content and generic explanation differ in more than mental-state wording alone.

The24-person pretest concerns perceptions of depicted deception. It neither validates the taxonomy as independent mechanisms nor tests actual deceptive robot execution, receiver harm or mitigation by justification.
Reported after-response trust and repeated blame are different designs. Only the latter is explicitly measured before/after in this summary; no automatic temporal trust-repair inference.

Machine consciousness, functional capacity, presented signal, recipient belief and ethical permission require separate evidence. An unsettled internal-state question must not become a definitive deception label by assumption.
Care examples are not clinical evidence or instructions to withhold information. The source’s practical hopes do not justify bypassing consent, privacy, task scope, oversight or remedies.
A separate publication is not automatically an independent participant cohort. Related summaries/later full articles must retain possible overlap and version limits.

Superficial/hidden labels distinguish the direction of a misleading capacity claim. External-world lying remains in the existing deception record; overlapping labels for one event are not multiple observed failures.

cross_paper_learning.finding: The later full article provides detailed norm-conflict experiments and, in its third experiment, repeated trust ratings. This early summary has only post-response trust in its stated sequence. Keep the publications’ scope and potential participant overlap distinct.

A belief that robots can never have human hallmarks is not itself evidence that a particular capability claim is deceptive. Verify capability truth and actual misleading cues; human dignity does not depend on the classification.

A robot described as capable of feeling pain can influence allocations without demonstrating actual pain or deceptive intent. Distinguish experimentally assigned information, beliefs and real system capacities.
Normative justification and posthoc rationalization are related but not synonyms. A later reason can be valid or misleading; timing alone does not prove dishonesty or recover the true cause.

deferred.term: External state deception as another ordinary-lying row
deferred.reason: Retain as a source-named distinction in Strategic deception. It concerns external-world misleading claims already covered there; no extra independent mechanism is established.
A planned intervention/research question, not a completed experimental effect in this report.

deferred.term: Deception objection as a psychological behavior
deferred.reason: A philosophical debate about whether and when social robot cues are deceptive, not a new measured behavioral construct.

deferred.term: Actual robot emotions or lack of all internal states
deferred.reason: The source stipulates/debates the issue and measures human perceptions. No consciousness measurement supports a new factual machine-mind conclusion.

limitations: Two named conceptual deception forms added; four measured/reported existing constructs and two non-counted contextual boundaries enriched. Catalogue becomes 771 records in eleven categories with stable IDs and unnumbered rows. Seven evaluation criteria and six principles unchanged. No invented counts, harm edges, source quota, full-paper Markdown archive, clinical recommendation or independent replication claim.
